newsitem.title: FIJI: Fiji Sugar Corp rejects strikers' safety claims.
newsitem.headline: Fiji Sugar Corp rejects strikers' safety claims.

text.p: Fiji Sugar Corp (FSC) on Monday rejected a claim by 2,500 unionists that they were striking over health and safety standards in Fiji's sugar mills.

Members of the Fiji Sugar and General Workers Union, which struck earlier Monday in all four of Fiji's sugar mills, said they were striking in support of a 3.5 percent pay rise and establishment of a welfare fund, as well as over health and safety standards in the mills.
FSC chief executive Jonetani Galuinadi said the health and safety claim was a ploy to avoid the strike being declared illegal by the Labour Ministry.
FSC's pre-strike forecast had been for the production of 440,000 tonnes of raw sugar in 1997, down from 475,000 tonnes in 1996.
The 1997 crush had been running well, with crushed cane showing higher sugar content than in 1996, before the strike began, Galuinadi said earlier on Monday.
Cyclone Gavin hit Fiji's canefields in March.
